svg.text: the transmit clock, and the FFE's tap weights

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: swing set by the standard; de-emphasis eats into it

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Where the margin is spent before the channel

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The transmit equaliser is deliberately a filter the signal passes through, so it is placed before the driver, not after it. Its

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: taps are set from a link training exchange or from a fixed preset, and every decibel of de-emphasis is a decibel of peak amplitude

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the driver must still be able to produce.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The output is AC-coupled almost everywhere, which is why the termination and the coupling capacitors appear in the path rather than

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: beside it. Their corner frequency is part of the low-frequency budget, and a long run of identical bits is what tests it.
